:project_name: Ansible Role "Manage Base"
= {project_name}

Special purpose Ansible role to manage fundamental setups and configurations that are shared across "factory" environments.

== What it does

`tasks/main.yml` runs these steps in order:

. Installs `geerlingguy.pip`, `geerlingguy.docker` (with the compose plugin) and `gesinn.manage_traefik`
  (`ensure-roles.yml`).
. Checks that no Docker network overlaps a subnet of the host (`check-docker-networks.yml`).
. Limits the journald retention with a drop-in in `/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/` (`configure-journald.yml`).
. Optionally configures a proxy for the Docker daemon and the Docker client (`setup-proxy.yml`).

Steps 2 to 4 are skipped when Docker, systemd or the proxy settings are not present. The Docker network check and the
journald step can be switched off.

== Requirements

* ansible-core 2.19 or newer (the CI tests the 2.19 floor and the latest release)
* Ubuntu (jammy, noble) or Debian (bullseye, bookworm)
* The roles listed in `requirements.yml`, pinned to the tested versions. Install them with
  `ansible-galaxy role install -r requirements.yml`.
* Privileges: run the play with `become: true`

== Usage

[source,yaml]
----
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Setup base environment
      ansible.builtin.include_role:
        name: gesinn.manage_base
      vars:
        manage_base_setup_proxy: true
----

Single task files can be called with `tasks_from`, for example `check-docker-networks.yml`. The task file names are part
of the interface of the role.

== Variables

[cols="2,1,3",options="header"]
|===
| Variable | Default | Description

| `manage_base_docker_network_check`
| `true`
| Run the Docker/host subnet overlap check.

| `manage_base_docker_network_check_mode`
| `fail`
| `fail` aborts on an overlap, `warn` only prints a warning.

| `manage_base_configure_journald`
| `true`
| Deploy the journald retention drop-in.

| `manage_base_setup_proxy`
| `false`
| Configure the proxy for the Docker daemon and client. Only effective when `proxy_env` defines `http_proxy` and
  `https_proxy`.

| `manage_base_docker_no_proxy`
| `elasticsearch,wiki,127.0.0.0/8`
| `noProxy` list in the Docker client config (`/root/.docker/config.json`).

| `proxy_env`
| `{}`
| Proxy environment (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`). Also used as `environment` while the dependency roles run.

| `docker_address_pools`
| `[]`
| `default-address-pools` for the Docker daemon. Existing networks are not changed retroactively.

| `journald_max_retention`
| `7day`
| `MaxRetentionSec` of the journald drop-in.

| `journald_system_max_use`
| `500M`
| `SystemMaxUse` of the journald drop-in.

| `journald_system_max_file_size`
| `50M`
| `SystemMaxFileSize` of the journald drop-in.
|===

`proxy_env`, `docker_address_pools` and the `journald_*` variables intentionally have no `manage_base_` prefix: they are
shared inputs that other roles read as well. They will be renamed with a major release.

== Handlers

`Restart docker` (after a changed proxy drop-in) and `Restart journald` (after a changed retention drop-in). Consumers
may define handlers with the same name in their play.

== Deprecated

* `tasks_from: fix-python-EXTERNALLY_MANAGED.yml` is now `fix-python-externally-managed.yml`. The old name still
  works and is removed with the next major release.

== Development

[source,shell]
----
make lint       # ansible-lint, production profile
make molecule   # all scenarios; ANSIBLE_CORE=2.19 runs the floor, SCENARIO=<name> runs one
----

The Molecule scenarios stub the dependency roles, `docker`, `ip` and `systemctl` (`molecule/shared`). Installing
packages, a real Docker daemon and systemd are therefore not covered by the tests.
